threads.topic: When Blaby draws its first new borrowing

entries.q: The capital strategy says external borrowing will likely be drawn once rates fall to around 5%. PWLB 5-year is 5.59% and 10-year 6.07%. What happens if rates do not reach 5% before the cash runs down?
entries.why: £13.7m of under-borrowing has to be funded eventually. A stated rate trigger the market does not reach turns into either a deferred capital programme or borrowing the strategy did not plan for.

threads.topic: The internal borrowing carry is narrowing

entries.q: Investments fell £3.0m to £20.4m and their return from 4.34% to 4.10%, while the CFR rose £1.5m. On present trends, when does cash stop covering the borrowing need?
entries.why: Internal borrowing is only free while there is cash to borrow internally, and the balances that make it work are being drawn down.

threads.topic: Refinancing at three times the current rate

entries.q: The book is £4.0m at 2.08% with 16.8 years average life; new borrowing is at 5.59% (5y) or 6.07% (10y). What borrowing rate does the MTFS assume?
entries.why: Financing costs are already 8.90% of net revenue on a book costing 2.08%. New debt at three times that rate changes the affordability arithmetic.

summary.text:
A district council that has funded its capital programme almost entirely from its own cash. At 31 March 2026 it held £21.6m of capital financing requirement against £4.0m of actual borrowing — all of it PWLB, all of it old, at an average 2.08% with 16.8 years to run. The gap is the story: £13.7m under-borrowed on the council's own prudential indicator, and £17.6m if finance leases are set aside.

That gap is currently profitable. The council earns 4.10% on £20.4m of investments while paying 2.08% on its debt, so internal borrowing is not a cost but a carry. The position is narrowing from both ends: investments fell £3.0m in the year and the return on them dropped from 4.34% to 4.10%, while the CFR rose £1.5m. No new borrowing was taken in 2025/26 and £0.858m was repaid.

The council has said when it intends to borrow. Its capital strategy states that as reserves and balances diminish over the life of the MTFS it will be necessary to draw new borrowing, and that external borrowing will likely be drawn once rates fall to around 5%. That is a stated trigger, not an inference — and PWLB is not there: the 5-year maturity rate fixed at 5.59% and the 10-year at 6.07% on 11 August 2026.
